newsitem.title: JAPAN: TENNIS-JAPAN'S DATE SAYS WILL RETIRE AT END OF SEASON.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-JAPAN'S DATE SAYS WILL RETIRE AT END OF SEASON.

text.p: Japan's top female tennis player Kimiko Date announced on Tuesday she will call it quits when the current season ends, saying she has achieved all she can.
"I came to think that now is the limit of my strength," Date said.
Ranked seventh in the latest Women's Tennis Association (WTA) rankings, Date has been one of the few Japanese to rise to such lofty heights in the world of professional tennis.
The 25-year-old Date said she first began thinking of retiring in June when the WTA announced a new, more severe, world ranking method.

Date said the most memorable moments during her career were when she defeated world champion Steffi Graf during the Federation Cup in April, and her play at Centre Court in the Wimbledon semifinal in July.
"I have no regrets... I was able to achieve things which I never dreamed of when I started playing tennis," Date said.
Date said she has not decided what to do after her final match in November. "But I'm not announcing my retirement to get married," she said.
She turned professional in 1989 after ranking in the top four in the All Japan Championship in 1987.
Date became the first Japanese woman in 21 years to reach a Grand Slam semifinal in the 1994 Australian Open and to enter the top 10 world rankings.
Date's final match will be the November WTA Championship in November.
